decisions.reason: As a standard handle family in the firm's core architectural hardware range, it remains inexpensive to carry and its continued presence suggests enough ongoing specification value to keep the option open.

The mitred handle family broadens the design offer for architects and planners, and with no negative signal reported the firm would likely retain it while learning whether it becomes a recurring specification choice.

This multifunctional handle is the most specialized offer here, so exit risk is higher if uptake stays limited, but it still fits the firm's accessibility and system-solution strategy well enough to justify continued market presence.
Because this lever-handle line sits close to established competencies and likely shares tooling, certifications and sales channels, the cost of keeping it remains low relative to its option value.
Its dedicated product positioning and prior German Design Award are strong indicators of market relevance, making withdrawal within the coming year unlikely.
A finish variant has low carrying cost and supports specification-driven architectural projects, so the firm would normally keep it unless clear evidence emerged that demand was persistently weak.
